facts.raw_span: A 5‐year‐9‐month‐old, 170‐kg domestic llama mare was referred for a 1‐week history of dyspnea and inspiratory noise
dyspnea and inspiratory noise
an esophageal obstruction had been suspected by the referring veterinarian, but spasmolytics and passage of a gastric tube did not improve the signs
the llama was bright, alert, in good condition (body‐condition score 3.5/5) with normal vital signs
a 10 × 8 × 3‐cm subcutaneous mass that was partially firm and fluctuant, slightly painful, and mildly warm
No dysphagia, other masses, or lymphadenopathy were detected
mild leukocytosis (23,690/µL; reference 8,700–17,500/µL) with neutrophilia (92.4%; reference 42.4–76.4%) and lymphopenia (3.0%; reference 7.0–32.5%)
eosinophils were decreased
hematocrit was 39.8% (reference 27.0–39.0%)
MCV was mildly increased, and MCHC was mildly decreased
Flexible endoscopy of the esophagus and trachea under sedation revealed no abnormalities
Cervical ultrasonography showed a well‐demarcated, heterogeneously echogenic, encapsulated mass with no communication with the trachea or esophagus and no intrinsic vascular flow
